waypoints.name: Whitney Portal
waypoints.directions: From US 395 in Lone Pine, turn west at the stoplight onto Whitney Portal Road and drive about 13 miles to its end at Whitney Portal. A Mount Whitney Zone permit is required for both day and overnight trips on this route, and human waste must be packed out.

waypoints.name: Mount Whitney
waypoints.directions: Start up the Whitney Trail and leave it where it crosses the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, about a mile up. Follow the climbers' path up the North Fork and over the Ebersbacher Ledges to Lower and Upper Boy Scout Lakes, then over slabs to Iceberg Lake. Climb the couloir above to the notch, then the steep final gully and face on the north side to the summit plateau.

waypoints.name: Meysan Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 in Lone Pine, turn west on Whitney Portal Road and drive about 11 miles to the signed Meysan Lakes Trailhead parking on the south side of the road, just past the Whitney Portal Campground turnoff. Parking is limited, and the trail is reached on foot through the campground. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive the Tioga Road (Hwy 120) to Tuolumne Meadows and park in the Cathedral Lakes trailhead lot beside the Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center; roadside parking at the trail's original start is not allowed. A short connector trail leads west to the Cathedral Lakes trail. A Yosemite entrance fee applies.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Peak
waypoints.directions: Start up the Cathedral Lakes trail (John Muir Trail) and within the first half mile branch onto the climbers' trail along Budd Creek, which stays on the west side of the creek and ends east of the Southeast Buttress after about 1,500 ft of gain. Scramble west through the trees to the base of the buttress and climb about five pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Saddlebag Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Conness
waypoints.directions: From the dam, follow use trails southwest past the old Carnegie Institute station to the north side of Alpine Lake, then climb northwest to the East Ridge and follow it west to the broad summit plateau. Cross the plateau and drop down the sandy gully marked by a large cairn, then talus, to the base of the West Ridge, and climb the ridge (about 12 pitches, mostly 4th class with moves to 5.6) back to the summit.

waypoints.name: Saddlebag Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US 395 at Lee Vining, drive west on Hwy 120 (Tioga Road) about 10 miles and turn right (north) onto Saddlebag Lake Road, about 2 miles before the Tioga Pass entrance. Follow this narrow, one-lane gravel road with turnouts about 2.5 miles to the parking area by the dam at the south end of Saddlebag Lake, near 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Leavitt Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-395 at Sonora Junction, about 17 miles north of Bridgeport, turn west on CA-108 and drive about 7 miles to Leavitt Meadows Campground. Overnight hiker parking is at the lot just as you enter the campground. A Hoover Wilderness permit is required for overnight trips.

waypoints.name: Tower Lake
waypoints.note: The usual camp for the climb, below Tower Pass.
waypoints.directions: Walk through the campground, cross the West Walker River on the footbridge and follow the West Walker River Trail south past Lower and Upper Piute Meadows, turning at the signed junction in Upper Piute Meadows to climb to Tower Lake.

waypoints.name: Tower Peak
waypoints.directions: From Tower Lake climb gravel, talus and grass south to Tower Pass, where the peak comes into view, and cross the basin beyond. Go up slabs beside a lingering snow patch to the northwest ridge, then leave the ridge onto its west side and traverse into the Northwest Chute, scrambling class 3 up it to the summit, about 2,250 ft above the lake.

waypoints.name: Bear Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Estes Park, take US 36 to the Beaver Meadows entrance of Rocky Mountain National Park, turn left onto Bear Lake Road just past the station and drive about 9 miles to the Bear Lake parking area at the road end. A park pass is required, and in the busy season Bear Lake Road needs a timed-entry reservation; the lot fills early, and a shuttle runs from the Park and Ride about 5 miles up the road.

waypoints.name: Arrowhead
waypoints.directions: Take the connector down to the Glacier Gorge trail, turn left at the junction for Mills Lake and continue past Jewel Lake to Black Lake. Skirt the right side of the lake, climb the boulder field and grassy slopes behind it on an intermittent path, traverse left on grassy ledges toward the valley between McHenrys Peak and Arrowhead, then scramble slabs to the long ramp that angles up right and around the north side of the summit.

waypoints.name: Devils Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Bend, follow the Cascade Lakes Highway west about 29 miles and turn left (south) at the sign for the Devils Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a Central Cascades Wilderness permit is required for day and overnight use during the summer permit season. Leave a second car at the Pole Creek Trailhead first.

waypoints.name: South Sister
waypoints.directions: Cross the highway and follow the South Sister climbers' trail about 1.5 miles up through forest, across a trail junction and onto the open plateau below the South Ridge. Climb the ridge on steep scree past the Lewis Glacier's moraine lake to the crater rim and follow the rim around to the summit.

waypoints.name: Middle Sister
waypoints.directions: Descend South Sister's Northwest Ridge on snow or scree and drop to the saddle with Middle Sister above Camp Lake, then climb large talus to Middle Sister's summit.

waypoints.name: North Sister
waypoints.directions: Descend north on snow or scree, steep snow or ice early in the season, along the upper edge of the Collier Glacier to the Prouty Point saddle. Climb loose slopes onto North Sister's ridge on paths that alternate between west-side ledges and the east side at gaps, cross the exposed Terrible Traverse snowfield, climb the loose Bowling Alley gully, and move up and right to the summit block.

waypoints.name: Pole Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Reverse the ridge to the Prouty Point saddle, descend the lateral moraine on the north side of the Hayden Glacier, and follow a climbers' path down beside a creek to the Pole Creek Trail. Cross Soap Creek and follow the trail past the Green Lakes junction and through the old burn to the trailhead, roughly 5 miles from the saddle.

waypoints.name: Happy Isles Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive into Yosemite Valley on Hwy 41, 140 or 120 and follow Southside Drive east toward Curry Village. Private cars cannot drive to Happy Isles; park in the trailhead parking near Curry Village and walk or ride the valley shuttle to the Happy Isles stop. A park entrance fee applies, and overnight trips need a Yosemite wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Mount Clark
waypoints.directions: Hike the Mist Trail or John Muir Trail past Vernal and Nevada Falls into Little Yosemite Valley, then follow the Merced Lake trail east past Bunnell Point. Leave the trail near its high point beyond Bunnell Point and climb southeast cross-country up one of the steep drainages below Mount Clark, through forest, slabs and talus, to the broad toe of the northwest ridge, then follow the exposed class 4 arete to the summit.

waypoints.name: West Village Lodge
waypoints.directions: From Bend, follow Century Drive, which becomes the Cascade Lakes Highway, west about 22 miles to Mt. Bachelor and turn into the West Village base area parking lot.

waypoints.name: Mount Bachelor
waypoints.directions: From the West Village base area, follow the signed summit hiking trail up through the ski area, on service roads and forest trail across the ski runs, then switchback up the steep, rocky upper ridge to the summit. This is a summer hike; in winter the mountain is an operating ski area.

waypoints.name: Timberline Lodge
waypoints.directions: From US 26 just east of Government Camp, turn north on Timberline Road and drive about 6 miles to the parking lots at Timberline Lodge. Fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the climbers' register in the Wy'east Day Lodge before starting. An Oregon Sno-Park permit is required to park from November through April.

waypoints.name: Mount Hood
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' trail on the east edge of the ski runs past the Silcox Hut and the top of the Palmer lift at about 8,500 ft. Continue up the snowfield toward Crater Rock, past Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, and swing around its east side to the base of the Hogsback. Follow the snow ridge to the bergschrund, climb the Old Chute to the summit ridge, and walk east to the top.
